title: FatPipe Constellation: Bringing It All Together for Modern Networks
summary: Device discovery is a key part of network monitoring, supported by network topology visualization, device inventory, and poller management.
body_markdown:
**Connecting FatPipe’s expertise in connectivity with visibility into the networks you depend on**


Device discovery is a key part of network monitoring, supported by network topology visualization, device inventory, and poller management. Understanding these individual features is only the starting point. This second part of our device discovery series takes a closer look at the technical aspects, connecting FatPipe Constellation’s capabilities with their practical applications.


**From Device Discovery to a More Useful Inventory**


Once discovered devices are added to[FatPipe Constellation’s](https://www.fatpipeinc.com/products/fatpipe-constellation) monitored inventory, administrators have a centralized view of their network assets and associated information. Network topology adds another dimension by showing device relationships and connections, helping administrators understand what equipment exists and how it fits into the wider network.


**Beyond Discovery: Monitoring What Matters**


Every network has its own monitoring requirements, and identifying devices sets the stage. FatPipe Constellation allows administrators to tailor[monitoring](https://www.fatpipeinc.com/products/fatpipe-total-security-360) to their infrastructure by creating custom device types and OID templates that define which SNMP objects to monitor. MIB files can be imported into Poller Configuration, making their definitions available through the MIB Object Tree, where administrators can browse and locate the required objects. The poller then uses the OIDs defined in the templates to collect information from the associated devices.


This flexibility extends to interface monitoring, bandwidth monitoring, hardware monitoring, configuration management, and WMI management. Rather than relying exclusively on generic device information, administrators can configure monitoring around the equipment they operate and the measurements that matter most to their organization.


**The Value of Knowing What to Monitor**


The real value of device discovery emerges when administrators put the information it produces to work. A discovered switch, for example, becomes more useful when its inventory details, interface status, bandwidth utilization, and hardware health can be examined together. FatPipe Constellation connects these capabilities within a centralized monitoring environment, helping IT teams apply the appropriate level of monitoring to different network devices.


For customers evaluating the platform, this provides a more meaningful basis for technical discussions and product demonstrations. Beyond determining whether Constellation can discover their equipment, they can explore how it can help them monitor and manage that equipment as their network evolves.


**Deep Domain Expertise for Modern Networks**


Helping school districts, healthcare organizations, and enterprises maintain an accurate understanding of their networks is an ongoing focus for FatPipe. New devices are introduced, existing equipment is replaced, and monitoring requirements change.


Device discovery and inventory help administrators keep track of network assets, while topology visualization provides context about their connections. Custom device types and reusable OID templates make it easier to establish consistent monitoring for similar equipment without defining every measurement from scratch. FatPipe[EnterpriseView](https://www.fatpipeinc.com/products/enterprise-view) brings monitoring information from distributed environments into a centralized view, allowing administrators to examine network health, device performance, and operating conditions across locations.


Ultimately, the goal is to simplify the work of managing complex networks. FatPipe Constellation’s capabilities work together to help administrators make sense of their network environment. Their value comes from how administrators use them to understand the equipment, connections, and conditions across their own networks.
